components: Linearizability: enforces read and write policy
links: replicate update to Read replica A

report control data to Consistency controller

steps: A write is invoked while the object contains v1.
At one instant between invocation and response, the object becomes v2.
The completed write establishes a real-time boundary.
Any later read must observe v2 or a newer value.

lesson.scenario: Two clients update and read one inventory register while a primary orders operations.

steps.title: Initial register
steps.narration: The primary stores stock 5 at version 21.
steps.invariant: A linearizable register has one legal sequential history.

steps.title: Write begins
steps.narration: Writer A invokes a conditional decrement.
steps.outcome: The operation is in flight and has not yet taken effect.
steps.invariant: The linearization point must lie between invocation and response.

steps.title: Write linearizes
steps.outcome: Stock 4 becomes the only current value.
steps.invariant: No reader may observe a partial atomic update.

steps.title: Response precedes read
steps.narration: The write completes before Reader B starts.
steps.outcome: Real-time order constrains the later read.
steps.invariant: If A completes before B begins, B must be ordered after A.

steps.title: Read sees latest
steps.narration: Reader B receives stock 4 from version 22.
steps.outcome: The observed result matches the real-time sequential history.
steps.invariant: A completed write cannot be hidden from a later linearizable read.
